q: Why does fresh snow sparkle?

a1: Each snowflake has flat, shiny sides. Sunlight bounces off them like lots of tiny mirrors.
a2: As you move, different bits catch the light, so it twinkles.
ask_back: Can you guess if snow sparkles more in sun or in shade?

q: Why is snow soft but ice is hard?
variants: how come snow is soft and ice is hard
why is snow all soft and fluffy but ice is hard if they are both frozen water
a1: Snow has lots of air between tiny bits of ice. Ice is packed solid with no air in it.
a2: Squash snow hard, and it starts to turn into ice.
ask_back: Do you think a packed snowball is closer to snow or to ice?

q: Why does snow by the road turn gray?
variants: how come the snow is dirty by the road
why is the snow next to the road all brown and gray and yucky
a1: Cars spray dirt, salt and water onto it. As it melts, the dirt stays behind and piles up.
a2: Snow in a quiet park stays white much longer.
ask_back: Can you guess where the whitest snow near you would be?

q: Why does snow turn into slush?
variants: how come the snow is all wet and mushy
why does the snow turn into icy watery slush when it gets a bit warm
a1: When it gets a little warm, snow starts to melt. Water and bits of ice mix into slush.
a2: Salt on roads makes slush happen even faster.
ask_back: Do you think slush is better for snowballs or for splashing?

q: Why do people put salt on icy roads?
variants: how come they put salt on the ice
why do trucks throw salt on the roads when it snows
a1: Salt makes ice melt, even when it's cold. Salty water has to get much colder to freeze.
a2: That stops roads from getting slippery for cars and people.
ask_back: Can you guess what happens to an ice cube with salt on it?

q: Why is the ice on a puddle white with bubbles?
variants: how come the frozen puddle has white bits
why is the ice on the puddle all white and cracks when i step on it
a1: Sometimes the water under the ice drains away and leaves air. Then the ice is thin and white, with air under it.
a2: That kind of ice cracks easily with a crunch.
ask_back: Can you guess if clear ice or white ice is stronger?

q: Why does ice form on top of a pond first?
variants: how come the pond freezes on the top
why does the ice on the pond grow on the top and not at the bottom
a1: The top of the pond touches the cold air first. So the top freezes first, and the ice floats there.
a2: The ice then grows thicker, a little at a time, downward.
ask_back: Do you think a small pond or a big lake freezes first?

q: Why doesn't a pond freeze all the way down?
variants: why pond not frozen at bottom
how come fish dont freeze in the pond
why doesnt the whole pond turn to ice in winter
why bottom of pond not ice
a1: The ice on top works like a lid that keeps cold out. The water at the bottom stays just above freezing.
a2: Fish and frogs rest down there all winter.
ask_back: Can you guess what the fish do under the ice?

q: Why can't I walk on the ice on the pond?
variants: why not walk on the pond ice
how come i cant go on the frozen lake
why is it not safe to walk on the ice on the pond when it looks frozen
a1: The ice can be thin in spots and crack. The water under it is very, very cold.
a2: Only a grown-up who checks the ice can say it's safe.
ask_back: Do you think ice near the edge or in the middle is thinner?

q: Why does ice on a lake make strange sounds?
variants: how come the frozen lake goes boom
why does the ice on the lake make pew pew and booming sounds
a1: Ice shrinks and grows as it cools and warms. It cracks, and long ice can sing and boom.
a2: The sounds travel far through the ice, like a big drum.
ask_back: Can you guess if the ice sounds louder at night or in the day?

q: Why do grown-ups scrape ice off the car?
variants: how come we have to get the ice off the car
why does a grown-up scrape the ice off the windows before driving
a1: The ice makes the windows hard to see through. A grown-up who drives must see well to stay safe.
a2: Cars can also blow warm air on the glass to melt it.
ask_back: Do you think ice comes off faster with warm air or with scraping?

q: Why does hail bounce?
variants: how come hail jumps on the ground
why does hail bounce all over the place when it hits the ground
a1: Hail is hard balls of ice, so they bounce like marbles. Snow is soft and fluffy, so it doesn't bounce.
a2: Hail can bounce off cars with a loud clatter.
ask_back: Can you guess if hail bounces more on a road or on grass?

q: Why is some hail so big?
variants: how come hail can be as big as a ball
why are some hailstones huge like golf balls and some tiny like peas
a1: Strong winds in a storm cloud hold hail up high. It keeps catching icy water and grows layer by layer.
a2: Cut a big hailstone, and you can see rings like an onion.
ask_back: Do you think big hail comes from a small cloud or a tall one?

q: Why can it hail in summer?
variants: how come there is ice falling when it is hot
why does it hail in the summer when it is so warm outside
a1: Summer storm clouds are very tall, and their tops are freezing. Hail falls fast, so it doesn't all melt on the way down.
a2: That's why hail often comes with thunder.
ask_back: Can you guess why hail melts fast once it lands?

q: Why do glaciers look blue?
variants: how come the ice is blue in the mountains
why is the ice in a glacier so blue and not white like snow
a1: Glacier ice is squashed so tight that it has very little air. Thick, clear ice soaks up red light, so blue is left.
a2: Snow on top has lots of air, so it still looks white.
ask_back: Do you think a thin piece of glacier ice looks blue or clear?

q: Why does snow look blue in the shade?
variants: how come the snow looks blue sometimes
why does the snow look a bit blue in the shadows
a1: Shady snow gets light from the blue sky, not the sun. Deep snow also soaks up a bit of red light.
a2: In sunshine, snow looks bright white again.
ask_back: Can you guess what color snow looks at sunset?

q: Why does snow fall so slowly?
variants: why does snow float down slowly but rain falls really fast
a1: Snowflakes are light and flat, so the air slows them down. Raindrops are heavier and fall much faster.
a2: They can spin and float side to side as they fall.
ask_back: Can you catch a snowflake before it lands?

q: Why are snowflakes sometimes big and fluffy?
variants: how come the snow is in big clumps
why are the snowflakes huge and fluffy some days and tiny on other days
a1: When it's not too cold, snowflakes stick together in big bunches. In very cold air, flakes stay tiny like dust.
a2: Big fluffy snowflakes are good for making a snowman.
ask_back: Do you think big snowflakes come on warm or very cold days?

q: Why does snow melt on the road first?
variants: how come the snow melts on the road but not the grass
why does the snow go away on the road but stay on the grass
a1: Dark roads soak up sunlight and warm up. Cars and road salt help melt the snow too.
a2: Grass stays cold and holds snow much longer.
ask_back: Can you guess if snow melts first on a dark car or a white car?

q: Why does my breath freeze on my scarf?
variants: how come my scarf gets frozen
why does my scarf get ice on it where i breathe when it is really cold
a1: Your breath is warm and has water in it. The cold scarf freezes that water into tiny ice.
a2: The ice shows up right where you breathe the most.
ask_back: Do you think this happens more on very cold days or warm ones?

q: Why is it bright at night when there is snow?
variants: how come its so light outside when it snows at night
why is it not dark outside at night when there is snow everywhere
a1: White snow bounces back light from street lamps and the moon. Clouds then bounce some light down again.
a2: So the whole night looks softly lit up.
ask_back: Do you think a snowy night is brighter with or without clouds?

q: Why are there winters with no snow?
variants: why does it not snow every winter even when it is cold
a1: Snow needs cold air and wet air at the same time. Some winters are too warm or too dry for snow.
a2: Some places almost never get snow at all.
ask_back: Do you think snow comes more on cloudy days or sunny days?

q: Why does snow pile up next to walls?
variants: how come there is lots of snow by the fence
why is the snow really deep by the wall but not much in the middle
a1: Wind blows the snow along until something blocks it. Behind walls and fences, the snow drops into big piles.
a2: These deep piles are called snow drifts.
ask_back: Do you think the deep snow is on the windy side or the other side?

q: Why does snow slide off the roof?
variants: how come the snow slides down the roof
why does the snow on the roof slide off with a big whoosh
a1: A warm house melts the bottom of the snow a little. That wet layer lets the whole pile slide down.
a2: That's why it's safe to stay away from the edge of roofs.
ask_back: Can you guess if snow slides faster off a steep roof or a flat one?

q: Why do clouds move across the sky?
variants: how come the clouds are moving
why do the clouds go across the sky when i watch them
a1: Wind high up pushes the clouds along. Up high, wind is often faster than down here.
a2: In a storm, clouds can race across the sky.
ask_back: Can you guess which way the wind blows by watching clouds?

q: Why do clouds look like animals?
variants: why cloud look like a dog
how come i see shapes in the clouds
why do some clouds look like animals and faces and dragons
a1: Clouds have puffy shapes that keep changing. Your brain loves to match shapes to things it knows.
a2: People also see faces in rocks, trees and even toast.
ask_back: Can you find a cloud that looks like an animal?

q: Why do clouds change shape?
variants: how come the cloud was a bunny and now it isnt
why does the cloud keep changing shape when i look at it
a1: Wind pulls and stretches the clouds. Edges dry up while new puffs grow in other spots.
a2: A cloud is never still, even when it looks still.
ask_back: Do you think fast wind changes clouds faster or slower?

q: Why are some clouds dark on the bottom and white on top?
variants: why cloud dark at the bottom
how come the clouds are gray underneath
why is the top of the cloud white and the bottom dark gray
a1: The sun lights up the top of the cloud. A thick cloud blocks the light, so the bottom is in shadow.
a2: The thicker the cloud, the darker the bottom looks.
ask_back: Is it a thick dark cloud or a thin white one that brings rain?

q: How do clouds hold so much water?
variants: how come rain clouds dont drop all their water
how does a big rain cloud hold all that water up in the sky
a1: A cloud's water is in tiny drops spread over a huge space. Rising air helps hold those tiny drops up.
a2: When drops join and get heavy, they fall as rain.
ask_back: Do you think a big gray cloud holds more water than a small white one?

q: Why are some clouds high and some low?
variants: how come some clouds are way up and some are close
why are some clouds really high up and others low down
a1: Clouds form wherever air gets cool enough to make drops. Some places that happens near the ground, some very high.
a2: Very high clouds are so cold they are made of ice.
ask_back: Can you guess which clouds move fastest, high ones or low ones?

q: Why do puffy clouds have flat bottoms?
variants: why clouds flat on the bottom
how come clouds are flat underneath
why do the fluffy clouds look flat at the bottom like they sit on a table
a1: The bottom is where rising air gets cool enough to make drops. Under that, the water stays in the air, too small to see.
a2: All the puffy clouds nearby often have bottoms at the same height.
ask_back: Can you see if nearby clouds have flat bottoms in a line?

q: Why do some clouds look like stripes?
variants: how come the clouds look like ripples
why do some clouds make rows and stripes across the sky
a1: Wind makes waves in the air, like waves on water. Clouds form on the tops of the waves, making stripes.
a2: Some people call these ripple clouds.
ask_back: Do you think it's windy up high when clouds make stripes?

q: Where do clouds go when they disappear?
variants: how come the cloud went away
why do clouds just disappear when i watch them
a1: Dry air mixes in, and the tiny drops dry up. The water is still there, but now you can't see it.
a2: It can make a new cloud in another place.
ask_back: Can you watch a small cloud and see if it fades away?

q: Can I touch a cloud?
variants: what does a cloud feel like
if i go really high up can i touch a cloud with my hand
a1: Yes, if you walk in fog, you are inside a cloud! It feels cool and damp, not fluffy like cotton.
a2: People on tall mountains often walk right through clouds.
ask_back: Do you think your hair would get wet in a cloud?

q: Why can't we sit on a cloud?
variants: why cant i sit on a cloud
how come clouds cant hold me
why cant you stand on a cloud like in cartoons
can i jump on a cloud
a1: A cloud is just tiny water drops floating in air. You would fall right through it, like through fog.
a2: Clouds look solid from far away, but they are not.
ask_back: Can you guess what a cloud would look like from the inside?

q: Why does fog go away later in the morning?
variants: why does the fog go away when the morning gets later
a1: The sun warms the air, and the tiny drops dry up. Wind can also blow fog away.
a2: Thick fog may last all day if the sun can't get through.
ask_back: Do you think fog goes away faster on sunny or cloudy days?

q: Why is it hard to see in fog?
variants: how come i cant see far in the fog
why is everything all white and hidden when it is foggy
a1: Fog is made of lots of tiny water drops. They bounce light every which way, so far things get hidden.
a2: Close things look clear, but far things fade away.
ask_back: Can you guess how far you can see on a foggy day?

q: Why does fog sit in low places?
variants: how come the fog is down low
why is there fog by the river and the fields but not up the hill
a1: Cold air is heavy and slides down into low places. Fog forms in that cold air, like milk in a bowl.
a2: Rivers and ponds add even more wet air there.
ask_back: Do you think a hill or a valley gets more fog?

q: Why does fog make my hair wet?
variants: how come my clothes get wet in the fog
why is my hair all wet when i walk in fog even though its not raining
a1: Fog is made of tiny water drops floating in the air. They land on you as you walk through.
a2: Lots of tiny drops add up to a wet coat.
ask_back: Can you guess if fog makes spider webs wet too?

q: Why do cars turn on their lights in fog?
variants: how come cars have lights on in the day when it is foggy
why do cars put their lights on when there is fog
a1: Lights help other drivers see the car in the fog. Fog hides cars that have no lights on.
a2: Drivers also go slowly in fog to stay safe.
ask_back: Do you think bright lights or dim lights are better in fog?

q: Why are there water drops on spider webs in the morning?
variants: how come spider webs have drops on them
why is the spider web covered in little water beads in the morning
a1: At night, the web gets cold, and water from air sticks. The drops line up on the threads like beads.
a2: This water is called dew.
ask_back: Can you find a web with dew drops on a cool morning?

q: Why is there no dew on cloudy nights?
variants: how come the grass is dry some mornings
why is the grass not wet in the morning after a cloudy night
a1: Clouds work like a blanket and keep the ground warmer. The grass doesn't get cold enough to make drops.
a2: Clear, still nights make the most dew.
ask_back: Do you think a windy night makes more dew or less?

q: Why does dew dry up in the morning?
variants: how come the grass gets dry later
where does the wet on the grass go when the sun comes up
a1: The sun warms the grass, and the drops dry into the air. Shady grass stays wet longer.
a2: By lunchtime, most dew is gone.
ask_back: Can you guess where dew stays the longest in your yard?

q: Why are there clouds on top of mountains?
variants: how come mountains have clouds on top
why do clouds sit on the top of the mountain like a hat
a1: Wind pushes air up the mountain, and it cools. Cool air makes clouds, so they hug the top.
a2: Some mountains wear a cloud like a hat.
ask_back: Do you think it rains more on mountains or flat land?

q: Why are some clouds puffy like cotton?
variants: how come clouds look like cotton candy
why are some clouds big and puffy and white like popcorn
a1: Puffy clouds grow from bubbles of warm air going up. Each bubble makes a new round lump on top.
a2: They often grow on warm days with lots of sun.
ask_back: Can you guess if a puffy cloud is growing or shrinking?

q: Why are some clouds thin and wispy?
variants: how come some clouds look like feathers
why are some clouds really thin and stringy high up in the sky
a1: Very high clouds are made of tiny ice bits, not drops. Fast winds up there stretch them into long wisps.
a2: Some people call them mares' tails.
ask_back: Do you think wispy clouds are higher or lower than puffy ones?

q: Why does it get cooler when a cloud covers the sun?
variants: how come it gets cold when the sun goes behind a cloud
why do i feel colder when a cloud goes in front of the sun
a1: The cloud blocks some sunshine, so less warmth reaches you. When it moves on, you feel warm again.
a2: Big thick clouds block more sun than thin ones.
ask_back: Can you guess how fast it gets cooler when a cloud covers the sun?

q: Why are there some days with no clouds at all?
variants: why are there no clouds at all in the sky some days
a1: On those days, the air is dry or slowly sinking. Sinking air warms up, so clouds can't form.
a2: Those days are often sunny and calm.
ask_back: Do you think a day with no clouds will be warm or cold at night?

q: Why do cloud shadows move on the ground?
variants: why shadow move on the hill
how come cloud shadows run across the field
why are there big dark shadows moving over the grass from the clouds
a1: A cloud blocks the sun and makes a shadow below. The wind moves the cloud, so its shadow moves too.
a2: On windy days, cloud shadows race across hills.
ask_back: Can you race a cloud shadow across a field?

q: Why do some clouds get so big and tall?
variants: how come clouds grow so tall
why do some clouds grow up and up like a giant tower
a1: Strong warm air pushes up fast and builds a tall cloud. These tall clouds can make thunder and big rain.
a2: Their tops can spread out flat, like an anvil.
ask_back: Do you think a tall cloud means storms or sunshine?

q: Why is lightning zigzag?
variants: how come lightning is all crooked
why does lightning go zigzag and not just straight down
a1: Lightning finds its way through the air in little steps. Each step goes a bit of a different way, so it zigzags.
a2: It also splits into branches, like a tree upside down.
ask_back: Can you draw lightning with lots of little zigzag steps?

q: Why does thunder rumble for so long?
variants: why does the thunder go on and on and rumble for ages
a1: Lightning is very long, so sound comes from near and far parts. The far parts' sound gets to you later.
a2: Sound also bounces off hills and clouds and comes back.
ask_back: Do you think close thunder sounds like a crack or a rumble?

q: Why does the wind howl?
variants: how come the wind sounds like a ghost
why does the wind make a whooo noise around the house at night
a1: Wind rushing past the edges of houses makes a whistle. The faster the wind, the louder the howl.
a2: It works like blowing across the top of a bottle.
ask_back: Can you make a howl by blowing across a bottle top?

q: Why does lightning hit tall things?
variants: how come lightning strikes the tallest things
why does lightning hit tall trees and towers more than the ground
a1: Lightning takes the easiest way to the ground. Tall trees and towers are closer to the cloud.
a2: That's why in a storm you go inside, not under a tree.
ask_back: Can you guess the tallest thing near your home?

q: Why does far-away thunder sound like a low rumble?
variants: how come thunder far away is quiet and grumbly
why does the thunder sound soft and rumbly when the storm is far away
a1: High, crackly sounds fade fast as they travel far. Low sounds go farther, so far thunder grumbles.
a2: Close thunder sounds like a sharp crack or bang.
ask_back: Do you think the storm is coming closer if the thunder gets louder?

q: Why should we go inside when there is thunder?
variants: why go inside in a storm
how come we cant play outside when it thunders
why do we have to come in when we hear thunder
a1: If you can hear thunder, lightning is close enough to hit. A house or a car is the safest place.
a2: Wait a while after the last thunder before going back out.
ask_back: Can you guess why a car with a metal roof keeps people safe?

q: Why do storms happen on hot summer days?
variants: how come it storms after a hot day
why does it get stormy in the afternoon when it was hot all morning
a1: Hot sun warms the ground, and warm, wet air rises fast. It builds tall clouds that make storms.
a2: That's why summer storms often come in the afternoon.
ask_back: Do you think a summer storm comes more in the morning or afternoon?

q: Why is the air cool after a storm?
variants: how come it feels cold after the storm
why is the air so cool and fresh after a big rain storm
a1: Cold air rushes down out of the storm cloud. Rain cools the ground and the air too.
a2: It can feel like someone opened a big fridge.
ask_back: Can you guess if the ground feels cooler after rain?

q: Why is wind cold sometimes and warm other times?
variants: how come the wind is warm today
why is the wind sometimes freezing and sometimes warm
a1: Wind brings air from other places. Wind from cold places is cold; wind from hot places is warm.
a2: Wind from the sea can feel cool on a hot day.
ask_back: Do you think wind from snowy mountains is warm or cold?

q: Why does wind make me feel cold?
variants: how come i get cold when its windy
why do i feel so cold when the wind blows on me
a1: Wind blows away the warm air hugging your skin. So a windy day feels colder than a still day.
a2: A coat holds warm air in, so wind can't take it.
ask_back: Can you guess why people turn their backs to cold wind?

q: Why does wind come in gusts?
variants: how come the wind blows hard then stops
why does the wind go whoosh then quiet then whoosh again
a1: Air tumbles around houses and trees, like water over rocks. So it speeds up and slows down in bursts.
a2: Hills and buildings make wind gustier.
ask_back: Can you count how long it is between gusts?

q: Why does the wind stop at night sometimes?
variants: how come its windy in the day and calm at night
why does the wind go away in the evening
a1: In the day, warm air rises and stirs up wind. At night, the stirring stops, so it often gets calm.
a2: Strong winds from big weather can still blow at night.
ask_back: Do you think it's calmer at night or at lunchtime where you live?

q: Why is it so windy between tall buildings?
variants: how come its windy next to big buildings
why does the wind blow so hard between the tall buildings downtown
a1: Wind squeezes between buildings and speeds up. Tall buildings also push wind down to the street.
a2: It works like water rushing through a narrow spot in a river.
ask_back: Can you guess if a corner or the middle of a street is windier?

q: Why do trees bend in the wind?
variants: how come trees move in the wind
why do the trees bend and wave when it is windy
a1: Wind pushes on all the leaves like a big sail. Trees can bend, so they move with the wind and don't break.
a2: Trees without leaves in winter catch less wind.
ask_back: Do you think a thin tree or a thick tree bends more?

q: Why do tornadoes spin?
variants: how come twisters go round and round
why does a tornado spin around so fast
a1: Winds blowing different ways in a big storm start the air spinning. The spin gets tight and fast, like a skater pulling arms in.
a2: Scientists are still learning just how tornadoes start.
ask_back: Can you spin faster with arms out or arms in?

q: Why do typhoons have an eye in the middle?
variants: how come the middle of a typhoon is calm
why is there a quiet hole in the middle of a typhoon
a1: The wind spins so fast it can't get into the middle. In the middle, air sinks slowly, so it stays calm. The sky can even be blue there for a while.
a2: Then the strong wind comes back from the other side.
ask_back: Do you think the eye is big or small next to the whole storm?

q: Why do typhoons start over the sea?
variants: how come typhoons come from the ocean
why do typhoons and hurricanes grow out over the warm sea
a1: Typhoons need warm sea water to grow. Over land, they lose their warm water and slowly get weaker.
a2: They grow in places where the sea is warm like a bath.
ask_back: Can you guess why typhoons come mostly in summer and autumn?

q: Why do typhoons have names?
variants: how come the typhoon has a name like a person
why do people give names to big storms and typhoons
a1: Names help people talk about each storm without mixing them up. A short name is easier to say than numbers.
a2: The names are picked from lists made ahead of time.
ask_back: Can you guess what name you would give a storm?

q: Why do typhoons bring so much rain?
variants: why does a typhoon make it rain so so much
a1: Typhoons pull up lots of warm, wet sea air. All that water falls as heavy rain on land.
a2: That is why grown-ups get ready before a typhoon comes.
ask_back: Can you guess what people do to get ready for a big storm?

q: Why is lightning so bright?
variants: how come lightning lights up the whole sky
why is lightning so so bright it hurts my eyes
a1: Lightning makes the air hotter than the outside of the sun. Air that hot glows very, very bright.
a2: The flash is over in less than a blink.
ask_back: Do you think lightning is brighter at night or in the day?

q: Why does lightning sometimes stay inside the clouds?
variants: how come the clouds light up
why do the clouds flash but i cant see the lightning bolt
a1: Most lightning jumps inside a cloud or between clouds. It lights the cloud up like a lamp.
a2: Only some lightning comes down to the ground.
ask_back: Can you guess why a cloud glows when lightning is inside it?

q: Can lightning strike the same place twice?
variants: can lightning hit the same spot again
is it true lightning never strikes twice in the same place
a1: Yes, it can! Very tall towers get hit many times each year.
a2: Tall, pointy things get hit the most.
ask_back: Do you think a tall tower or a small house gets hit more?

q: Why does thunder make the windows shake?
variants: how come the house shakes when it thunders
why do the windows shake when there is really loud thunder
a1: Thunder is a big push of air that travels out fast. That push can rattle windows and doors.
a2: Very close thunder can even shake the floor a little.
ask_back: Can you guess if close or far thunder shakes windows more?

q: Why is there strong wind just before a storm?
variants: how come it gets windy before it rains
why does the wind blow really hard right before the storm comes
a1: Rain and cold air rush down out of the cloud. When they hit the ground, they spread out as strong wind.
a2: This cool gust tells you the rain is close.
ask_back: Do you think the rain comes right after the wind or much later?

q: Why does the air smell funny before a storm?
variants: how come it smells weird before the storm
why does the air smell sharp and clean right before a thunderstorm
a1: Lightning makes a gas with a sharp, clean smell. Wind can carry that smell ahead of the storm.
a2: After the rain starts, the rain smell joins in.
ask_back: Can you guess if your nose can tell a storm is coming?

q: Why do leaves spin in a little whirlwind?
variants: how come the wind makes a little tornado of leaves
why do the leaves go round and round in a little spinning wind
a1: Hot ground warms the air, and it rises in a spin. It picks up leaves or dust and twirls them.
a2: They are called dust devils, and most are small.
ask_back: Can you guess if dust devils come on hot days or cold days?

q: Why do people count after lightning?
variants: how come we count till the thunder
why do grown-ups count the seconds between the lightning and thunder
a1: Counting tells how far away the storm is. Every three seconds is about one kilometer.
a2: Light gets to you right away, but sound takes time.
ask_back: Can you count the seconds next time you see lightning?

q: Why can I see lightning but not hear thunder?
variants: how come i see lightning but no sound
why can i see flashes far away but i dont hear any thunder
a1: The storm is so far that its thunder fades on the way. You can see a flash much farther than you can hear it.

ask_back: Do you think that storm is near or far from you?

q: Why do big storms knock trees down?
variants: how come the storm broke the tree
why do trees fall over when there is a big storm
a1: Strong wind pushes very hard on the tree. Wet, soft dirt holds the roots less tightly.
a2: Old or sick trees fall over more easily.
ask_back: Can you guess if a tree with leaves or without leaves catches more wind?

q: Why is some lightning purple?
variants: why is the lightning sometimes purple or blue and not white
a1: Lightning is mostly white, but rain and dust can change its color. Far-away lightning can look pink or purple.
a2: Scientists still study why it changes color.
ask_back: Do you think lightning looks the same color every time?

q: Why does wind make a flag flap?
variants: how come flags wave in the wind
why does the flag go flap flap flap when it is windy
a1: Wind swirls behind the flag, pushing it one way then the other. That makes it ripple and flap.
a2: Stronger wind makes the flag flap faster and louder.
ask_back: Can you guess which way the wind blows by looking at a flag?

q: Why do storm clouds look green sometimes?
variants: how come the clouds look green
why does the sky go a funny green color before a big storm
a1: Very tall, thick storm clouds can make light look green. Scientists are not fully sure why.
a2: It often happens late in the day when sunlight is orange.
ask_back: Do you think a green sky means a big storm or a small one?

q: Why does wind blow my umbrella inside out?
variants: how come my umbrella goes inside out
why does the wind turn my umbrella upside down
a1: Wind pushes up under the umbrella and flips it. The thin frame bends when wind pushes the wrong way.
a2: Pointing the umbrella into the wind helps.
ask_back: Can you guess which way to tip an umbrella on a windy day?

q: Why do storms move?
variants: how come the storm goes away
why does the storm go from one place to another place
a1: Winds high up push the whole storm along. So a storm can come, pass over, and go.
a2: Some storms move fast, and some move slowly.
ask_back: Can you guess which way a storm is moving by watching the clouds?

q: Why can't I touch a rainbow?
variants: why cant i touch a rainbow
how come i cant catch the rainbow
why does the rainbow move away when i try to walk to it
a1: A rainbow is not a thing; it's sunlight coming from raindrops. It moves when you move, so you can never reach it.
a2: Every person sees the rainbow in a slightly different spot.
ask_back: Do you think a rainbow would still be there if you walked into the rain?

q: Why do I sometimes see two rainbows?
variants: how come there is a double rainbow
why is there another rainbow on top of the first rainbow
a1: Light can bounce twice inside raindrops. That makes a second, fainter rainbow outside the first.
a2: In the second rainbow, the colors are flipped!
ask_back: Can you guess which color is on top in the second rainbow?

q: Where does a rainbow end?
variants: how come i cant find the end of the rainbow
where is the end of the rainbow
a1: A rainbow has no end you can reach. It's really a full circle, and the ground hides the bottom half.
a2: From a plane, people can sometimes see a whole round rainbow.
ask_back: Do you think a rainbow from a mountain top looks rounder?

q: Why are rainbow colors always in the same order?
variants: how come red is always on top of the rainbow
why are the colors in the rainbow always the same way round
a1: Each color bends a different amount in the raindrops. Red bends the least, so it's always on the outside.
a2: Violet bends the most, so it's on the inside.
ask_back: Can you say the rainbow colors from the outside in?

q: Why is a rainbow always on the other side from the sun?
variants: how come the sun is behind me when i see a rainbow
why do i only see the rainbow when the sun is behind me
a1: Sunlight goes into raindrops and comes back out toward you. So the sun must be behind you to see one.
a2: Look at the rain, not at the sun.
ask_back: Can you guess where to look for a rainbow in the late afternoon?

q: Why do rainbows fade away?
variants: why does the rainbow fade away after a little while
a1: The rain stops, or the sun goes behind a cloud. Without both sun and raindrops, the rainbow can't show.
a2: That's why rainbows often last only a few minutes.
ask_back: Do you think a rainbow lasts longer in light rain or heavy rain?

q: Why can I make a rainbow with a garden hose?
variants: how to make a rainbow with water
how come the hose makes a rainbow
why is there a rainbow in the water spray from the hose
a1: The hose spray makes tiny drops, just like rain. Sunlight in the drops makes the rainbow.
a2: Stand with the sun behind you and spray the water up.
ask_back: Can you make a rainbow with water and sunshine?

q: Why is the sky brighter inside a rainbow?
variants: how come it is bright under the rainbow
why does the sky look lighter inside the rainbow and darker outside
a1: Raindrops send more light back inside the rainbow. Outside the bow, less light comes back to you.
a2: Between two rainbows, the sky looks extra dark.
ask_back: Can you see a bright sky inside the next rainbow?

q: Why don't we see rainbows at lunchtime?
variants: how come rainbows come in the morning or evening
why do rainbows only come when the sun is low
a1: The sun must be low in the sky to make a rainbow. When the sun is high, the rainbow hides below the ground.
a2: Early morning and the end of the day are the best times.
ask_back: Do you think a rainbow in the evening is high or low in the sky?

q: Can you see a rainbow at night?
variants: can the moon make a rainbow
can you see rainbows at night when the moon is out
a1: Yes, a very bright moon can make a faint moonbow. It often looks white, because our eyes see few colors at night.
a2: You don't see them often, so they are special.
ask_back: Do you think a full moon or a thin moon makes a moonbow?

q: Why are there rainbows near waterfalls?
variants: why is there always a rainbow in the spray from a waterfall
a1: Waterfalls throw tiny drops into the air all the time. When the sun shines on them, a rainbow appears.
a2: You can see these rainbows even on days with no rain.
ask_back: Can you guess what time of day is best for a waterfall rainbow?

q: Do two people see the same rainbow?
variants: do we see the same rainbow
is my rainbow the same as yours
if we both look at the rainbow do we see the same one
a1: No, each person sees light from different raindrops. So your rainbow is just for you!
a2: It moves with you when you walk.
ask_back: Do you think your two eyes each see a different rainbow?

q: Why is it colder in the morning than in the afternoon?
variants: how come it is cold in the morning and hot later
why is it so cold when i wake up but warm after lunch
a1: All night, the ground loses its warmth to the sky. The sun needs hours to warm everything back up.
a2: The coldest time is often just before the sun comes up.
ask_back: Can you guess the coldest time of the whole day?

q: Why is the afternoon the hottest time of day?
variants: how come its hottest after lunch
why is it hotter in the afternoon than at lunchtime when the sun is high
a1: The ground keeps soaking up sun all morning. Heat builds up, so it's warmest a bit after lunch.
a2: It's like a pot that keeps getting hotter on the stove.
ask_back: Do you think it's hotter at breakfast or after lunch?

q: Why does it get warmer in spring?
variants: how come it gets warm in spring
why does the weather get warmer when spring comes after winter
a1: In spring, our part of Earth starts leaning toward the sun. Days get longer, and the sun climbs higher.
a2: More sun each day slowly warms the land.
ask_back: Can you guess what plants do when spring gets warm?

q: Why are some places hot all year?
variants: how come some countries are never cold
why is it hot all the time in some places and never snows
a1: Places near the middle of Earth get strong sun all year. They never lean far away, so winter never comes.
a2: Their days are about the same length all year too.
ask_back: Do you think it snows in places near the middle of Earth?

q: Why is it summer in some countries when it is winter here?
variants: how come its hot there and cold here
why do some people have summer at the same time we have winter
a1: The top and bottom halves of Earth lean opposite ways. When one half leans toward the sun, the other leans away.
a2: So some people go to the beach in winter months.
ask_back: Can you guess what season it is on the other half of Earth now?

q: Why do some places have a wet season and a dry season?
variants: how come it rains for months then stops
why do some places have lots of rain for months and then no rain
a1: Near the middle of Earth, it's warm all year. Instead, winds bring months of rain, then months of dry.
a2: Plants and animals there get ready for each season.
ask_back: Do you think plants look greener in the wet or dry season?

q: Why does the weather change so much in spring?
variants: how come it snows then is sunny in spring
why is the weather sunny one day and cold the next in spring
a1: In spring, cold air and warm air take turns pushing in. That brings sun, rain, and sometimes even snow!
a2: The warm air wins more and more as spring goes on.
ask_back: Can you guess why people say spring weather is hard to guess?

q: Why is it hot in summer even when it is cloudy?
variants: how come its hot and cloudy
why is it still really hot in summer even when there are clouds
a1: Clouds block some sun, but summer days are long and warm. The air and ground are already warm too.
a2: Clouds can also hold warm air in at night.
ask_back: Do you think a cloudy summer day is cooler than a sunny one?

q: Why are clear nights colder than cloudy nights?
variants: how come clear nights are so cold
why is it colder at night when there are no clouds in the sky
a1: Clouds work like a blanket over the ground. With no clouds, warmth floats away into the sky.
a2: That's why frost comes on clear nights.
ask_back: Can you guess if there will be frost after a clear winter night?

q: Why is there a longest day of the year?
variants: how come one day is the longest
why is there one day in summer that has the most daylight
a1: On that day, our half of Earth leans most toward the sun. After that, days slowly get shorter again.
a2: There is also a shortest day in winter.
ask_back: Can you guess what month has the longest day where you live?

q: Why does it get chilly in autumn?
variants: how come it gets cold in fall
why does the weather get cooler when it is autumn
a1: Days get shorter, so the sun has less time to warm us. Nights get longer, so more warmth leaks away.
a2: The sun also sits lower in the sky each week.
ask_back: Do you think autumn mornings or afternoons feel more chilly?

q: Why is it still hot at night in summer?
variants: how come its hot when i go to bed in summer
why is it so hot at night in summer when the sun is gone
a1: The ground and houses soaked up heat all day. They give it back slowly all night.
a2: Short summer nights don't give much time to cool down.
ask_back: Can you guess if a stone wall is warm in the evening?

q: Why do we get heat waves?
variants: how come its super hot for lots of days
why is it really really hot for days and days in a row
a1: Sometimes a big bubble of hot air sits still for days. The air in it sinks, warms, and keeps clouds away.
a2: Drinking water and staying in the shade helps in a heat wave.
ask_back: Can you guess why people use fans in a heat wave?

q: Why is it cold on a sunny winter day?
variants: how come its sunny but freezing
why is it so cold in winter even when the sun is shining
a1: Winter sun is low, so its light spreads thin over the ground. Short days don't give enough time to warm up.
a2: Snow also bounces sunlight away before it can warm things.
ask_back: Do you think the sun feels warmer at lunchtime or at sunset in winter?

q: Why does it only snow in winter?
variants: how come it doesnt snow in summer
why does it only snow in winter and never on hot days
a1: Snow needs freezing air all the way down to the ground. Summer air is too warm, so snow melts into rain.
a2: High mountains can get snow even in summer.
ask_back: Can you guess where snow might fall in summer?

q: Why do seasons take so long to change?
variants: how come summer takes so long to come
why does it take so long for winter to change to spring
a1: Earth takes a whole year to go around the sun. So each season lasts about three months.
a2: The change happens a little bit every day.
ask_back: Can you guess how many seasons fit in one year?

q: Why is it warm on some days in winter?
variants: how come its warm today when its winter
why is it sometimes warm like spring in the middle of winter
a1: Wind can bring warm air from far away for a few days. Then the cold air comes back.

ask_back: Do you think a warm winter day will melt snow?

q: Why does the north wind feel cold?
variants: how come wind from the north is freezing
why is the wind from the north so cold
a1: In the top half of Earth, north wind comes from colder places. In the bottom half, the south wind is the cold one!

ask_back: Can you guess which way the cold wind blows where you live?

q: Why is it cooler by the sea in summer?
variants: how come its not so hot by the sea
why does it feel cooler near the sea on a hot day
a1: Sea water warms up much more slowly than land. So breezes off the sea stay cool on hot days.

ask_back: Do you think a town by the sea or far away is hotter in summer?

q: Why do I feel hotter when the air is sticky?

a1: Sweat cools you when it dries. In wet air, sweat can't dry fast, so you stay hot.

q: How do we know when a new season starts?

q: Why are day and night the same length in spring and autumn?

why is the day as long as the night in spring and autumn

ask_back: Can you guess if days are getting longer or shorter right now?

q: Why does the weather change?

q: Why are some summers hotter than others?

why is it super hot some summers and not so hot other summers
a1: Each year, the winds and the sea change a little. Our world is also slowly getting warmer.

q: Why is it dark all day in winter near the North Pole?

why no sun in winter at the north pole

q: Why does the ground freeze in winter?

why is the dirt frozen and hard in winter

q: Why is it still cold at the start of spring?

why is it cold even though it is supposed to be spring

q: Why is the hottest part of summer after the longest day?

q: Why does the sun feel warm on a cold day?

q: Why do days get longer after winter?

a1: Earth moves around the sun and slowly leans us back toward it. Each day after the shortest day gets a bit longer.

ask_back: Can you guess if it gets dark earlier or later next month?

q: Why is the weather different in different places?

why is it hot in one place and cold in another place
a1: Places near the middle of Earth get the most sun. Being near the sea or high up changes weather too.

q: Why are pebbles on the beach so smooth?

why are the stones on the beach all smooth and not sharp
a1: Waves roll pebbles against each other for years and years. Their sharp corners slowly wear away.

a1: A little water makes the sand grains cling to each other. Too much water, and the sand turns runny again.

q: Why do some rocks have stripes?

why are there stripes in some rocks like a cake

q: Why do rocks look shinier when they are wet?

q: Why are some rocks heavy and some light?

q: Why are rocks different colors?

why are some rocks red and some gray and some white

q: Where do boulders come from?

where do the really really big rocks come from

q: Why is there a giant rock all alone in a field?

a1: Long ago, giant sheets of ice carried it there. When the ice melted, the rock was left behind.

q: Why do pebbles get smaller?

a1: Waves keep knocking them, and bits chip off. After a very long time, pebbles can turn into sand.

q: Why are river stones smooth?

why are the stones in the river so smooth and round
a1: River water tumbles stones along the bottom. Bumping and rubbing make them round and smooth.

q: Why are some stones flat?

why are some stones flat and good for skipping
a1: Some rocks split into thin, flat layers. Water then rubs them smooth.

q: Why do crystals have flat sides?

why do crystals have flat sides and pointy ends
a1: Their tiny bits line up in neat rows as they grow. That makes flat sides and sharp points.

q: Why are there crystals inside some rocks?

why does a rock look boring outside but has sparkly crystals inside

q: Why are diamonds so hard?

q: Why does dry sand run through my fingers?

a1: Dry sand grains are round and slide past each other. Nothing holds them together, so they pour like water.

q: Why is some sand black or pink?

why is the sand black at some beaches and pink at others

q: Why do rocks break?

why do rocks crack and break into smaller rocks
a1: Water gets into cracks, freezes, and pushes them wider. Plant roots and heat can crack rocks too.

q: Why is some dirt sticky like clay?

why is some mud sticky like play dough
a1: Clay is made of super tiny, flat bits. When wet, the flat bits slide and stick, like wet paper.

q: Why is sand scratchy?

why does sand feel scratchy in my shoes and on my legs
a1: Sand grains are tiny bits of hard rock with edges. Rubbing them on skin feels rough.

q: Why does dirt have little rocks in it?

why do i find little rocks when i dig in the dirt

q: Why do some rocks have holes in them?

q: Why is chalk soft?

q: Why does sand stick to my feet?

why is the wet sand cool when the dry sand is hot
a1: Water drying from the sand takes warmth away. Wet sand also gets cooled by the sea.
a2: That's why it feels nice to walk near the water.
ask_back: Can you guess if dry sand or wet sand is cooler on a hot day?

q: Why do my footprints disappear on the beach?
variants: how come my footprints are gone
why do my footprints in the sand disappear after a while
a1: Waves smooth the sand flat again. Wind blows dry sand into footprints, too.
a2: Footprints far from the water last longer.
ask_back: Can you guess how many waves it takes to wipe out a footprint?

q: Why can't I see the bottom of the lake?
variants: how come the lake is dark
why cant i see the bottom of the lake when it is deep
a1: Deep water and tiny bits in it block the light. Less light reaches the bottom, so it looks dark.
a2: Some very clear lakes let you see far down.
ask_back: Do you think it's easier to see the bottom on a sunny day?

q: Why does the sand make ripples under the water?
variants: how come the sand has lines like waves
why does the sand at the beach have little wavy lines
a1: Moving water pushes sand into little ridges. Wind does the same to sand in deserts.
a2: You can feel the ripples with your feet.
ask_back: Can you guess if the ripples point the way the water moves?

q: Why does the sea look like it ends far away?
variants: how come the sea looks like it stops
why does the sea look like it ends at a line far away
a1: Earth is round, so the sea curves away from you. That line is as far as your eyes can see.
a2: Ships far away seem to sink from the bottom up.
ask_back: Do you think you'd see farther from a tall tower?

q: Why do waves knock me over?
variants: how come the wave knocked me down
why do the waves knock me over when i stand in the sea
a1: A wave carries lots of heavy water moving fast. Even a small wave pushes harder than you think.
a2: That's why it's safest to swim with a grown-up watching.
ask_back: Can you guess if it's easier to stand sideways to a wave?

q: Why is the water lighter near the beach?
variants: how come the water is light blue near the sand
why is the sea light near the beach and dark far out
a1: Near the beach, the water is shallow, so the sand shows through. Deeper water looks darker blue.
a2: You can tell how deep water is by its color.
ask_back: Do you think dark water is deep or shallow?

q: Why do some rivers have rapids?
variants: how come the river is white and splashy there
why does the river get white and bumpy in some places
a1: Water rushes over big rocks and down steep spots. The rocks make it splash and foam white.
a2: Some people ride rapids in boats with helmets on.
ask_back: Can you guess if rapids are fast or slow water?

q: Why doesn't a pond have big waves like the sea?
variants: how come ponds dont have waves
why is the pond flat but the sea has big waves
a1: Wind needs lots of open water to build big waves. A small pond is too small for big waves to grow.
a2: Big lakes can have big waves, though.
ask_back: Do you think a huge lake can have waves like the sea?

q: Why is the tide higher on some days?
variants: how come the sea comes up higher some days
why is high tide really high some days and not others
a1: When the sun and moon line up, they pull together. That makes extra high and extra low tides.
a2: This happens at full moon and new moon.
ask_back: Can you guess if the tide is bigger at full moon or half moon?

q: Why do ponds smell?
variants: how come the pond smells bad
why does the pond smell yucky like rotten eggs
a1: Old leaves rot at the bottom of still water. Tiny germs breaking them down make a smelly gas.
a2: Ponds with moving water smell much less.
ask_back: Do you think a pond smells more in summer or winter?

q: How are lakes made?
variants: how come there is a lake there
how does a lake get made in the ground
a1: Water fills low places, like a giant bowl in the ground. Ice, rivers or volcanoes dug many of those bowls.
a2: Some lakes are made by people with dams.
ask_back: Can you guess where the water in a lake comes from?

q: Why does sand get so hot in the sun?
variants: how come the sand burns my feet
why is the sand at the beach so hot i have to run on it
a1: Sand soaks up sunshine, and the heat stays in the top layer. It can't pass the heat down fast.
a2: Dig down a little, and the sand is much cooler.
ask_back: Can you guess if dark sand or light sand gets hotter?

q: Why do caves have pointy rocks hanging down?
variants: how come caves have rock icicles
why are there rocks hanging from the roof of the cave like icicles
a1: Water drips from the cave roof and leaves tiny bits of rock. Drip by drip, over many years, they grow into icicle shapes.
a2: They grow very slowly, a tiny bit each year.
ask_back: Can you guess why we should not touch them?

q: Why do pointy rocks grow up from the cave floor?
variants: why rocks grow up in caves
how come there are pointy rocks on the cave floor
why are there rock spikes pointing up from the floor of the cave
a1: Drips land on the floor and leave rock bits there too. Sometimes the top and bottom meet and make a pillar.
a2: These ones are often fatter than the ones hanging down.
ask_back: Do you think the top and bottom ones grow toward each other?

q: Why are deserts cold at night?
variants: why is the desert so hot in the day and so cold at night
a1: Dry air and no clouds let the heat escape fast. With no blanket of clouds, nights get chilly.
a2: People in deserts often wear warm clothes at night.
ask_back: Can you guess if a desert night or a jungle night is colder?

q: Why do cliffs fall into the sea?
variants: how come the cliff falls down
why do bits of the cliff fall into the sea
a1: Waves crash into the bottom and slowly wear it away. With nothing holding it up, the top falls down.
a2: That's why it's safe to stay back from cliff edges.
ask_back: Do you think soft rock or hard rock cliffs fall faster?

q: Why are cliffs so straight up and down?
variants: how come cliffs go straight down
why is the cliff like a wall going straight up
a1: Waves or rivers cut the bottom away. Then the top breaks off in big flat pieces.
a2: Each break leaves a new straight wall.
ask_back: Can you guess if a cliff is getting closer to houses over time?

q: Why are caves cold inside?
variants: why is it cold inside a cave even in summer
a1: Deep underground, it stays cool all year. Caves feel cool in summer and warmer in winter.
a2: Bring a coat if you visit a cave.
ask_back: Do you think a cave feels warm or cool in winter?

q: Why are caves wet and drippy?
variants: why is there water dripping everywhere inside the cave
a1: Rain soaks down through cracks in the rock above. It drips from the cave roof and walls.
a2: Some caves even have rivers inside.
ask_back: Can you guess if caves drip more after rain?

q: How are caves made?
variants: how does a big hole get made inside the rock
how did the cave get there
a1: Many caves are carved by water slowly eating away soft rock. Some caves are tubes left by lava.
a2: Waves make caves in sea cliffs too.
ask_back: Do you think it takes a long or short time to make a cave?

q: Why are there big sand hills in the desert?
variants: how come there are big sand hills
why does the desert have big hills made of sand
a1: Wind blows sand and piles it into hills called dunes. The dunes slowly creep along as the wind blows.
a2: Some dunes are taller than big buildings.
ask_back: Can you guess which side of a dune is steeper?

q: Why does a canyon have stripes?
variants: how come the canyon walls are stripy
why are there colorful lines on the walls of the canyon
a1: The walls show layers of rock laid down over a long time. Each stripe was once a different layer of sand or mud.
a2: The bottom layers are the oldest.
ask_back: Can you guess if the top stripe or bottom stripe is older?

q: How did a river make a canyon?
variants: how come a river made a big hole
how can a little river cut a giant canyon in the rock
a1: The river cut down a tiny bit each year, for ages. Sand in the water scrapes the rock like sandpaper.
a2: The river is still at the bottom, cutting deeper.
ask_back: Do you think the canyon is still getting deeper?

q: Why are some valleys shaped like a V and some like a U?
variants: how come valleys are different shapes
why do some valleys look like a V and others like a U
a1: Rivers cut thin V-shaped valleys. Giant ice moving slowly cut wide U-shaped ones.
a2: So a U valley tells you ice was there long ago.
ask_back: Can you draw a V valley and a U valley?

q: Can a desert be cold?
variants: is it true some deserts are cold and snowy
a1: Yes, a desert is any place with very little rain or snow. Some icy places are deserts too.
a2: The coldest desert is at the bottom of Earth.
ask_back: Do you think a desert has to be sandy?

q: Why are there rock arches with holes through them?
variants: how come a rock has a big hole like a door
why are there rocks shaped like a bridge or a door
a1: Wind and water wear a hole through a thin rock wall. The hole grows into an arch.
a2: One day, the top may fall down.
ask_back: Can you guess what wears the hole bigger, wind or water?

q: Why are some desert rocks shaped like mushrooms?
variants: how come the rock is thin at the bottom
why are some rocks thin at the bottom and fat on top
a1: Wind blows sand low, so it scrapes the bottom most. The bottom wears thin, and the top stays wide.
a2: Soft rock at the bottom wears away faster too.
ask_back: Do you think a mushroom rock will fall over one day?

q: Why are some hills green and some brown?
variants: how come the hills are green here and brown there
why are the hills green in spring and brown in summer
a1: Green hills get lots of rain; brown ones are dry. In dry times, the grass dries up and turns brown.
a2: After rain, brown hills can turn green again.
ask_back: Can you guess what color the hills are after lots of rain?

q: Why do paths go zigzag up a hill?
variants: how come the road goes back and forth up the hill
why does the path go side to side up the mountain
a1: Zigzag paths are less steep, so it's easier to walk up. You walk farther, but it's not so hard.
a2: Roads up mountains zigzag for cars too.
ask_back: Do you think going straight up or zigzag is harder?

q: Why are there sandstorms?
variants: why does the wind blow sand into a big cloud in the desert
a1: Strong wind picks up loose, dry sand and carries it. Sand fills the air like a big brown cloud.
a2: People cover their faces to keep sand out.
ask_back: Can you guess why sandstorms happen more in deserts?

q: Why do big holes open in the ground?
variants: how come the ground fell in
why does a big hole suddenly open up in the ground
a1: Water can wash away rock under the ground. Then the top falls in, making a hole.
a2: These holes are called sinkholes, and most are small.
ask_back: Do you think soft rock or hard rock makes more sinkholes?

q: Why is there water in the desert sometimes?
variants: how come there is a pond in the desert
why is there a little lake with trees in the middle of the desert
a1: Water from deep underground comes up in a low spot. Plants and palm trees grow around it.
a2: This green spot is called an oasis.
ask_back: Can you guess why animals visit an oasis?

q: Why is desert sand red or orange?
variants: how come the desert sand is orange
why is the sand in some deserts red like rust
a1: Rust on the sand grains makes them red or orange. The rust comes from iron in the rocks.

ask_back: Do you think the sand color shows what rocks are nearby?

q: Why are there caves in sea cliffs?
variants: why are there holes and caves in the cliffs at the beach
a1: Waves pound weak spots in the cliff until they become caves. Rocks thrown by waves help dig them out.

ask_back: Can you guess why sea caves are wet inside?

q: Why does the road look wobbly on a hot day?
variants: how come the air looks wiggly over the road
why does the air above the road look all wavy when its hot
a1: The hot road heats the air above it. Light bends as it passes through the wiggly warm air.

q: Why does the road look wet on a hot day when it isn't?
variants: how come there is fake water on the road
why do i see puddles on the road far away that disappear
a1: Hot air near the road bends sky light up to your eyes. So you see the sky on the road, like water.
a2: This is called a mirage, and it moves as you move.
ask_back: Do you think you can ever reach the fake puddle?

q: Why do puddles steam after a summer rain?
variants: how come the road is smoking after rain
why does steam come off the ground after it rains on a hot day
a1: Rain lands on very hot ground and warms up fast. Warm water rises and turns into little drops in cooler air.

ask_back: Can you guess if dark roads or grass steam more?

q: Why does the pavement feel hot on my feet?
variants: how come the sidewalk burns my feet
why is the sidewalk so hot on my bare feet in summer
a1: Pavement soaks up sun all day and gets hot. Dark ground heats up faster than light ground.

ask_back: Do you think grass or pavement is cooler for bare feet?

q: Why is the road hotter than the grass?
variants: why is the road really hot but the grass next to it is cool
a1: Dark roads soak up lots of sunlight. Grass has water inside, which keeps it cool.
a2: Grass is also not dark like a road.
ask_back: Can you guess if a white path is cooler than a black road?

q: Why is it cooler under a tree?
variants: why does it feel cooler in the shade under a big tree
a1: Leaves block the sun and make shade. Leaves also let out water, which cools the air.
a2: A tree's shade can feel cooler than an umbrella's.
ask_back: Do you think big trees or small trees give better shade?

q: Why does the road get soft and sticky in summer?
variants: how come the road gets gooey
why is the black stuff on the road soft and sticky when it is hot
a1: Road tar is like thick goo that gets soft when hot. Cold makes it hard again.

q: Why does it feel hotter in the city?
variants: how come its hotter in town
why is it hotter in the city than in the park or the country
a1: Roads and buildings soak up sun and stay hot. Parks with trees and grass stay cooler.

ask_back: Do you think a park or a parking lot is cooler?

q: Why do sidewalks have lines and gaps?

a1: Sidewalks grow and shrink a tiny bit on hot and cold days. The lines make any cracks go there, not all over.

ask_back: Can you count the lines as you walk on the sidewalk?

q: Why do rocks get hot in the sun?
variants: why are the rocks so hot when the sun shines on them all day
a1: Rocks soak up sunshine and hold the heat. Dark rocks get hotter than light ones.

q: Why is it hot even in the shade on some days?

variants: how come houses are white in hot countries
why do people paint houses white where it is really hot
a1: White bounces sunlight away, so houses stay cooler. Dark colors soak up sunlight and get hot.

q: Why does the ground feel cool when I dig down?
variants: how come the dirt is cold under the top

a1: Only the top of the ground gets warmed by the sun. Deeper down, the dirt stays cool.

q: Can you cook an egg on the sidewalk?

a1: Usually not; sidewalks don't get quite hot enough. But they can get hot enough to hurt bare feet.

q: Why does hose water come out hot at first?

a1: The hose sat in the sun and warmed the water inside. Then cool water from underground pipes comes through.

q: Why does it get so dusty in summer?

q: Why is it cooler near a river or fountain?

why does it feel cooler near the river on a hot day
a1: Water warms up slowly, so it stays cooler than the ground. Drying water also takes warmth from the air.

q: Why does a puddle get warm in the sun?

why is the water in the puddle warm when the sun shines on it
a1: Shallow water warms up fast in sunshine. Deep ponds take much longer to warm.

q: Why is the sun so hot?

why is the sun hot all the time and never cools down
a1: The sun is a giant ball of very hot gas. Deep inside, tiny bits squeeze together and make lots of heat.

is the sun hotter than a oven
a1: The sun is much hotter than any fire or oven. Even its outside would melt any rock.

how come the sun is so big but looks so small

q: Why is it still light after the sun goes down?

why is the sky still bright when the sun went away already
a1: The sun still shines on the air high above us. That air spreads some light down to us.

q: Why does the sun look bigger when it is setting?

why the sun is bigger in the evening

how does the shadow clock tell what time it is
a1: A sundial has a stick that makes a shadow. As the sun moves across the sky, the shadow moves too.

q: Why doesn't a sundial work at night?

how come sundial don't tell time when it's dark
does a sundial work at night
a1: A sundial needs sunshine to make a shadow. At night there is no sun, so there is no shadow.

q: What is noon?
a1: Noon is twelve o'clock in the daytime. It is the middle of the day.

q: What is midnight?
a1: Midnight is twelve o'clock at night. It is when one day ends and the next begins.

q: What is dawn?
a1: Dawn is the early morning time when the sky starts getting light. It comes just before the sun pops up.

q: What is dusk?

a1: Dusk is the time just after the sun goes down. The sky is getting dark, but it is not night yet.

q: Why does the sky get light before the sun comes up?

why is it light in the morning but no sun yet
a1: The sun is not up yet where you are. But its light already reaches the air high above you.

q: Why does it get cooler in the evening?

why is it colder at night than in the day
a1: In the evening, the low sun warms the ground less. Then the ground slowly loses its heat.

q: Why is the sky lighter near the ground?

how come sometimes the sky is super blue and sometimes white
why sky not always same blue

q: Why is the sky orange when there is smoke?

q: Does a red sky at night mean good weather?

is red sky at night sailors delight true

why do people say red sky at night

q: Why does the sun feel hotter at lunchtime?

why sun hot at lunch time

q: Why is the sun yellow?

q: Why are days long in summer and short in winter?

how come it's still light at bedtime in summer
why dark so early in winter
a1: The Earth is tilted. In summer, your side leans toward the sun, so days are long.

q: Why does the sun come up in the east?

how come the sun always comes up on the same side
which way does the sun come up
a1: The Earth spins toward the east. As it turns, we see the sun first on the east side.

q: Does the sun move across the sky?

q: Is the sun on fire?

a1: Not like a campfire. The sun does not need wood or air like a fire does.

q: Why can I see sunbeams through the clouds?

why are there light beams in the sky
a1: Sunlight shines through gaps in the clouds. Dust and tiny drops light up, so you see beams.

q: Is it the same sun everywhere in the world?

does everyone have the same sun
